metadata.title: Jalen Coker - Practicing Friday
metadata.description: Coker (ankle) is in uniform and catching punts at Friday's practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Coker figures to continue playing through the ankle injury that he suffered in the first quarter of Carolina's Week 1 contest. It hasn't slowed him down so far, with Coker still handling a huge role on offense and also returning punts. He should be ready for the same role Sunday at Cleveland.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) doesn't practice Thursday
metadata.description: Jalen Coker (ankle) didn't take part in practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Coker was held out of Thursday's practice due to his ankle injury that has been bothering him for a while. He was able to practice on Wednesday, though, so it seems like this may just be an injury management move from the part of the team. Fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his status over the next 24 hours or so.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker - Listed as non-participant
metadata.description: Coker (ankle) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report.
metadata.analysis: After getting in a limited session Wednesday, Coker was unable to get any work one day later due to a lingering ankle issue. He was joined as a non-participant by fellow WR Xavier Legette (knee) on Thursday, leaving Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie as the other healthy options at the position behind No. 1 Tetairoa McMillan.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) not on field to start practice Thursday
metadata.description: Jalen Coker was on a bike to begin practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Coker was limited to begin the week on Wednesday. His status will need to be monitored when the official injury report is released.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker - Still bothered by ankle Thursday
metadata.description: Coker (ankle) was spotted using an exercise bike at the beginning of Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Coker was listed as limited Wednesday due to an ankle injury and seems likely to go down as limited again Thursday once the Panthers release their practice report. He experienced some practice limitations due to an ankle injury during the previous week but suited up for this past Sunday's win over the Falcons, in which Coker secured eight of nine targets for 66 yards. Coker and Tetairoa McMillan have been one of the league's most effective wide receiver duos to begin the season.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker Downgraded to DNP Thursday
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker (ankle) did not practice Thursday after opening the week as a limited participant. That's a step backward for Coker, who has been dealing with the ankle since rolling it in the season opener. He was limited twice last week before practicing in full Friday and playing against Atlanta, where he caught eight passes for 66 yards. Coker has been one of Carolina's most productive receivers through two games, totaling 16 catches for 204 yards and two touchdowns. Thursday's DNP doesn't rule him out for Sunday at Cleveland, but it puts more weight on what he is able to do Friday. If Coker can't go, John Metchie III would be one of the receivers in line for more work.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker Using an Exercise Bike During Practice
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker (ankle), who was limited in practice on Wednesday, was seen riding an exercise bike with a sweater on to begin practice on Thursday, according to Mike Kaye of The Charlotte Observer. Coker is likely to be listed as limited again, but if he can upgrade to a full practice on Friday, he could be cleared for the Week 3 tilt on the road in Cleveland against the Browns. The 24-year-old tweaked his ankle in the season-opening loss to the Chicago Bears but returned and went off for eight catches, 138 yards, and two touchdowns. Coker was active in the Week 2 blowout win over the division-rival Atlanta Falcons and once again had eight receptions on nine targets, but this time for only 66 yards. He is clearly still not over his ankle injury, but it does not seem like something that will keep him from playing or slowing him down in another potential blowup spot against the Browns. If Coker is active this weekend, fantasy managers need to find a way to get him in lineups.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker Proving That His High Volume is Not a Fluke
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker had an outrageously productive Week 1, but given his relatively low fantasy stock before the season started, managers wanted to wait and see whether he could replicate his production in Week 2. While he didn't have another 138-yard, two-touchdown performance, he proved that his volume is certainly sustainable from week to week. In fact, Coker has finished with exactly nine targets and eight catches in each of his two games so far. He has also played at least 76% of the snaps in both contests. It has been very encouraging to see the Panthers' passing attack firing on all cylinders, as both Coker and Tetairoa McMillan have been able to produce double-digit fantasy points (PPR) in each of the first two games. To this point, Coker ranks as the WR5 in PPR leagues with 33.8 and 14.6 points in the first two weeks, respectively. Bryce Young is playing the best football of his career, and nobody has benefitted more than Coker and his fantasy managers. He's firmly in must-start territory as a low-end WR2 for Week 3 against an unintimidating Browns defense.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) limited at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Jalen Coker (ankle) was limited at Carolina's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Coker was dealing with an ankle injury all last week, but he was able to play through it and put up a good performance on Sunday. He is still limited by it to start practice this week, but it looks like he again is expected to play through it in Week 3. Fantasy managers shouldn't hesitate to start him if he gets full clearance to play before the end of the week.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker - Limited with ankle issue Wednesday
metadata.description: Coker (ankle) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: An ankle injury slowed Coker in practice last week as well, but he was able to play through it and register eight grabs in the win over the Falcons. He was limited Wednesday, and this could be the norm for Coker during the week until he's back to 100 percent. At this stage, his availability for Sunday's game against the Browns does not appear to be in question.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker - Will remain on punt returns
metadata.description: Coach Dave Canales said Monday that Coker will remain the team's punt returner moving forward, Kassidy Hill of the Panthers' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: After the Panthers cut Jimmy Horn last week, Coker got the first crack at returning punts in Week 2, and he responded with returns of 13 and 36 yards against Atlanta. Canales said Coker earned a longer look after that performance. Adding return duties just gives Coker another path to scoring fantasy points, helping raise both his floor and ceiling.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker snags eight passes in win
metadata.description: Jalen Coker caught eight of nine targets for 66 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons.
metadata.analysis: Coker had some great grabs in this game, including some toe-tapping plays along the sideline. He and Tet McMillan are forming a promising duo for the Panthers, and Coker is worth starting every week.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker - Busy day in big win
metadata.description: Coker brought in eight of nine targets for 66 yards and returned two punts for 49 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Coker didn't generate the splash plays that were a big part of his Week 1 body of work against the Bears, but the speedy wideout led the Panthers in receptions and finished second to Tetairoa McMillan in both receiving yards and targets. Coker averaged a modest 8.3 yards per grab on the afternoon, yet his stellar catch rate -- he's brought in 16 of 18 targets through his first two games -- and sizable role in the air attack makes him a highly appealing option in all formats heading into a Week 3 road matchup against the Browns next Sunday.

metadata.title: Is Jalen Coker a Must-Start in Week 2 vs. Falcons?
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers wideout Jalen Coker is coming off his two biggest games of his young NFL career. He has combined for 17 catches for 272 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 21 targets in those outings. The 24-year-old was the PPR WR1 in overall scoring in Week 1 with 33.8 fantasy points. Heading into Week 2, Coker will face a stout Atlanta Falcons secondary featuring A.J. Terrell, Jessie Bates III, and Xavier Watts. The Falcons surrendered 221 passing yards and one touchdown against 41 passing attempts in Week 1 to the Pittsburgh Steelers. In a less-than-ideal matchup, Coker is RotoBaller's PPR WR27 this week. Coker has been a fantasy favorite in the community and is building his case as one of the league's better young receivers. He can be plugged into fantasy lineups as a viable flex option, but we should not expect him to repeat as a top-10 fantasy receiver in Week 2.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker Looking to Build Off Impressive Performance in Week 2
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue his strong play against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2. Coker logged a full practice on Friday and doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Falcons. The 24-year-old was seen in a walking boot on Monday, but was cleared after practicing throughout the week. He caught eight of nine targets for 138 yards and two touchdowns while playing 95% of the team's offensive snaps against the Bears in the regular-season opener. Coker showed a good rapport with quarterback Bryce Young and has 17 catches for 272 yards and two touchdowns over his last two games since the Wild Card loss to the Rams. Coker is ranked WR26 at RotoBaller and will keep things rolling against the Falcons, making him a strong WR3/FLEX heading into Week 2.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) logs full practice Friday
metadata.description: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker was a full participant in practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Coker began the week in a precautionary boot after he injured his ankle last Sunday against the Bears. He'll remain an upside WR3/flex play for fantasy managers heading into Week 2.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker - Cleared for Sunday's game
metadata.description: Coker (ankle) doesn't have a game designation for Sunday's matchup against Atlanta after participating fully in Friday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Coker didn't miss a beat last Sunday after rolling his ankle in the first quarter, and he's now managed a full practice after being limited the previous two days. He played 95 percent of Carolina's snaps Week 1 prior to sitting out the final drive in garbage time.

metadata.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) takes part in special teams drills to begin practice
metadata.description: Jalen Coker took part in special teams drills to begin practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Coker was limited in practice to begin the week. He appears on track to be good to go for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
